subject: Bounded processing & custody proposal — DPA follow-up
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stellarhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@stellarhealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:10:00 +0000
Subject: Quick follow-up: DPA carveouts + model improvement opt-out

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team impressed with the latency profile. Legal asked me to surface a few narrow requests they want reflected in the DPA before procurement can move to PO:

- A clear "no-model-improvement" commitment for tenant data used via the hosted API (no training, incremental updates, or fine-tuning).
- Explicit custody language for prompt/response artifacts (confirmation whether outputs are treated as Customer Confidential or considered derived system logs).
- A subprocessors list and an operational path for evidence (how do we prove no-training for a given retention window).

I've attached a short PDF with their requested snippets. Can we propose operational controls or a short addendum that addresses each point? Our timeline is tight — would love a short outline by Monday.

Appreciate it,
Sophie Turner
Enterprise Ops / StellarHealth

Attachment: Stellar_DPA_snippet_requests.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: DPA carveouts + model improvement opt-out

Sophie — thanks for sending these through and for the good conversation. Looping in Monica (Customer Security/Privacy) and David (Legal ops) so we can propose a concise operational addendum.

High-level responses up-front:
- No-model-improvement commitment: we can add a scoped clause for hosted API usage that prevents any of StellarHealth's tenant data from being used to update model weights, and we will maintain an immutable audit trail of model update events. We will also provide an attestation cadence (quarterly) and an on-demand evidence pack.
- Prompt/response custody: we treat generated outputs as customer-owned artifacts for customers who contract that entitlement; otherwise outputs are logged as ephemeral system telemetry. We'll sketch both options and the operational differences (SFTP export, retention window, encryption-in-transit and at-rest).
- Subprocessors & evidence: we'll provide a subprocessor snapshot with roles (inference, logging, storage) and an evidence path (audit logs + signed attestation + KMS residency statement).

We have a draft operational sketch attached — it's intentionally short and maps to each of the snippets you sent. Monica/David — can you review and add any blocking asks we should plan for before Monday?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: bounded_processing_sketch.v1.md (text, 12KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: DPA carveouts + model improvement opt-out

Thanks Karthik — reviewed the sketch and added notes inline (see bullets below). My priority is an evidenceable operational flow that procurement/legal can verify without needing to run an on-site audit. Key items: 

- Attestation scope & cadence: We can commit to a no-training attestation for tenant content if the customer opts into the entitlement. Attestations will include: model version IDs, timestamped KV-cache snapshots showing no weight-update events, and a signed audit log for inference jobs. Suggested cadence: quarterly + on-demand (subject to NDA).

- Live controls: Provide a tenant-level toggle to opt into "no-improvement" mode in the Console (this will ensure requests are routed to non-trainable fleets and disable any telemetry that could be consumed into training). Need engineering signoff for deployment timeline (2–4 weeks for gated release).

- Proof artifacts: exportable evidence pack containing: (1) subprocessor snapshot (timebound), (2) signed attestations, (3) export of inference audit logs (redacted), (4) KMS key metadata showing residency. For EU customers we can restrict to onshore storage; for StellarHealth (US), they want onshore residency + SFTP export option.

- Prompt/response ownership: Recommend adding two paths in the DPA: (A) Customer elects "Output Ownership" (customer owns outputs; Redwood will mark logs as customer-confidential and provide export tooling), (B) "Default" (outputs treated as ephemeral telemetry, retained per standard retention schedule). The DPA addendum should make the selection explicit and reversible only by amendment.

David — can your team draft contractual language for the addendum and a short checklist for procurement acceptance? I'll coordinate the Console toggle spec with Product/Eng if we get a PO.

—Monica
Director, Customer Security & Privacy

From: Legal <legal@stellarhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: DPA carveouts + model improvement opt-out

Karthik / Monica — thanks for the rapid responses and the sketch. A few clarifying questions from our side before we review a proposed addendum: 

1) Toggle mechanics: is the Console toggle enforced at request-routing time (i.e., requests tagged as "no-improvement" will be routed only to non-training pools with a strict forked telemetry pipeline)? We need guarantees about both routing and telemetry sanitation.

2) Evidence turnaround: for an on-demand attestation, what SLAs can Redwood commit to (e.g., 5 business days to provide signed attestations + audit logs)?

3) Subprocessor snapshot: can Redwood provide a timebound list and a signed manifest that includes vendor role, country, and last-verified timestamp? We may require the manifest be provided at signature and again at each quarterly attestation.

If you can answer these three items in a short email and include the proposed addendum language we can circulate to procurement. We prefer to avoid lengthy back-and-forth if we can get firm operational guarantees.

Best,
N. Legal (on behalf of StellarHealth)

--- Forwarded attachment: Stellar_DPA_snippet_requests.pdf
